Find the chromatic number of the following graphs.
(i) Complete Bipartite Graph
(ii) Complete Graph
(iii) Cycle graph
(iv) Wheel Graph
(v) Regular Graph

Nice — short, direct, no fluff. Answers and why:

# (i) Complete bipartite graph \(K_{m,n}\)
- **Chromatic number:** \(2\) (provided \(m,n\ge1\)).  
- **Why:** Vertices split into two independent parts; color one part with color A and the other with color B. If one part is empty (degenerate), \(\chi=1\).

# (ii) Complete graph \(K_n\)
- **Chromatic number:** \(n\).  
- **Why:** Every pair of vertices is adjacent, so each vertex needs a distinct color.

# (iii) Cycle graph \(C_k\) (cycle on \(k\) vertices, \(k\ge3\))
- **Chromatic number:** 
  - \(2\) if \(k\) is even,  
  - \(3\) if \(k\) is odd.  
- **Why:** Even cycles are bipartite (2-colorable). Odd cycles require 3 colors (they are not bipartite).

# (iv) Wheel graph \(W_n\) (a cycle of \(n-1\) rim vertices plus a central hub; \(n\ge4\))
- **Chromatic number:** 
  - \(4\) if \(n\) is even (i.e. rim has odd length),  
  - \(3\) if \(n\) is odd (i.e. rim has even length).  
- **Why:** If the rim is even → rim needs 2 colors, hub adjacent to both rim colors → needs a 3rd color. If the rim is odd → rim already needs 3 colors and the hub is adjacent to all three → needs a 4th.

# (v) Regular graph (every vertex has degree \(\Delta\); a “\(k\)-regular” graph means \(\Delta=k\))
- **Chromatic number:** Varies — there is no single value determined by regularity alone.  
- **Sharp bounds (Brooks’ Theorem):** For a connected \(k\)-regular graph,
  - \(\chi \le k\) **except** when the graph is \(K_{k+1}\) (complete) or an odd cycle (the \(k=2\) case); in those exceptions \(\chi=k+1\).  
- **Examples:** Even cycle (2-regular) → \(\chi=2\). \(K_{k+1}\) is \(k\)-regular and requires \(k+1\) colors.

If you want, I can:  
— give quick examples for each case, or

In simple and structured easy way

Here’s a **simple and structured** version 👇  

---

### **(i) Complete Bipartite Graph (Kₘ,ₙ)**
- **Chromatic Number:** 2  
- **Reason:**  
  Vertices can be divided into two groups where no edges are inside a group.  
  → Color one group with Color 1 and the other with Color 2.

---

### **(ii) Complete Graph (Kₙ)**
- **Chromatic Number:** n  
- **Reason:**  
  Every vertex is connected to every other vertex.  
  → Each vertex must have a different color.

---

### **(iii) Cycle Graph (Cₙ)**
- **Chromatic Number:**  
  - 2 → if n is even  
  - 3 → if n is odd  
- **Reason:**  
  Even cycles are bipartite (2 colors enough).  
  Odd cycles need one extra color (3 total).

---

### **(iv) Wheel Graph (Wₙ)**
- **Chromatic Number:**  
  - 3 → if n is odd  
  - 4 → if n is even  
- **Reason:**  
  The center vertex connects to all rim vertices.  
  - If rim is even → 2 colors for rim + 1 for center = 3  
  - If rim is odd → rim needs 3 + 1 for center = 4

---

### **(v) Regular Graph**
- **Chromatic Number:** Depends on the graph  
- **General Rule (Brooks’ Theorem):**  
  - ≤ degree of each vertex (k)  
  - = k + 1 only for complete graphs or odd cycles  
- **Example:**  
  - Even cycle (2-regular) → 2 colors  
  - Odd cycle (2-regular) → 3 colors  
  - Complete graph K₄ (3-regular) → 4 colors

---
